chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and others, who said:
The water (of semen) is the water of the man; he places it where he wills. However, if he brings forth a child, he does not deny it, and he is strict in denying the child.
ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined in Shia jurisprudence when a man's semen is deposited?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the legal principle of 'Ilqâ' (attribution of paternity) in Shia jurisprudence, asserting that semen is inherently linked to its owner regardless of location, yet paternity is established unless formally disavowed. It underscores the strictness ('shaddada') required in denying offspring, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving lineage and the presumption of legitimacy in cases of temporary marriage (Mut'ah). This ruling serves as a foundational text for understanding how biological connection translates into legal responsibility and inheritance rights within the family structure.
